title.en: Articles: a, an, the or nothing
title.es: Artículos: a, an, the o ninguno

summary.en: Use **a/an** for one of many things or when you first mention something. Use **the** when the listener knows which one: it was mentioned before, it is unique, or the context makes it clear. Use **no article** for plural or uncountable nouns when you speak in general: _Prices are rising_, _Life is expensive_.
summary.es: En español decimos «la vida» o «los precios» en general; en inglés, para generalizar, no se usa artículo: life, prices, people.

form: **a** + consonant sound (_a job_, _a university_); **an** + vowel sound (_an hour_, _an MBA_)
**the** + singular, plural or uncountable noun when it is specific or unique (_the sun_, _the report you sent_)
**no article** + plural or uncountable noun in general statements (_Doctors earn more than teachers_)
**the** + superlatives, _the first/last_, rivers, seas, mountain ranges, and countries with _Republic/Kingdom/States_

uses.text: **First mention** → a/an; **second mention** → the: _I bought a jacket and a scarf. **The** jacket was cheap._
**Unique or obvious things** → the: _the moon_, _the government_, _the city centre_.
**General statements** → no article: _Music helps me concentrate._ _People often work too hard._

note.en: Compare _Music helps me_ (in general) with _The music in this café is loud_ (specific).
note.es: Para hablar en general no uses the: «la música ayuda» = Music helps.

uses.text: **Jobs and descriptions** → a/an: _She is **an** engineer._ _He's **a** very patient man._
**Fixed expressions without an article**: _go to work_, _at home_, _in hospital_, _by train_, _at university_, _in bed_.
**Place names**: no article for most countries, cities and lakes (_Italy_, _Lake Garda_); **the** for plural names and groups (_the Alps_, _the Netherlands_, _the Atlantic_).

mistakes.wrong: The life is more expensive than before.
mistakes.right: Life is more expensive than before.

why.en: Do not use the when you talk about something in general.
why.es: En general no se usa the, aunque en español digamos «la vida».

mistakes.wrong: The people in my country are very friendly.
mistakes.right: People in my country are very friendly.

why.en: People in general takes no article. Use the only when it is a specific group: the people I met.
why.es: «La gente» en general es people, sin the.

mistakes.wrong: She is doctor at the hospital near here.
mistakes.right: She is a doctor at the hospital near here.

why.en: A singular job title needs a/an.
why.es: En inglés la profesión lleva a/an: «es médica» = she is a doctor.

mistakes.wrong: I go to the work by the bus every morning.
mistakes.right: I go to work by bus every morning.

why.en: Go to work and by + transport are fixed expressions with no article.
why.es: Expresiones fijas: go to work, by bus, at home.

examples.en: I saw a film last night. The film was about a lighthouse keeper.
examples.es: Anoche vi una película. La película trataba de un farero.

examples.en: Honesty is important in any relationship.
examples.es: La honestidad es importante en cualquier relación.

examples.en: Could you close the window? It's freezing in here.
My brother is an architect and my sister is a pilot.
She spends most of her free time at home.
The Danube flows through several countries.
We travelled to Spain by train.
Children learn quickly when they are interested.
It was the most boring lecture I've ever attended.
He's been in hospital since Monday.

practice.prompt: ___ coffee keeps me awake if I drink it late.

explanation.en: Coffee in general is uncountable and general, so no article is used.

practice.prompt: She's ___ engineer at a wind-farm company.

explanation.en: Engineer starts with a vowel sound, and a job title takes a/an.

practice.prompt: I had lunch with a colleague. ___ colleague recommended this restaurant.

explanation.en: The colleague was mentioned before, so we use the.

practice.prompt: Most ___ in this town travel to work by car.

explanation.en: People in general takes no article.
